key_insight: Incorporating patient-specific respiratory motion into a CT-informed Gaussian splatting renderer enables dynamic, phase-aware 3D visualizations that align endoscopic video to preoperative CT without breath-holds, reducing CT-to-body divergence by modeling airway deformation in real time.
problem_solved: Respiratory motion deforms airways by 5–20 mm, causing CT-to-body divergence that limits bronchoscopic localization accuracy; current breath-hold protocols are hard to reproduce and disrupt clinical workflow.
method: Build a volumetric Gaussian-splat representation of the airway derived from the patient’s preoperative CT.
Estimate or model patient-specific respiratory motion fields and apply them to deform the Gaussian splats across respiratory phases to create a dynamic CT-informed scene.
Render phase-consistent views and register live endoscopic video to the dynamic rendering for improved localization without requiring breath-holds.
impact: Enables more accurate, robust bronchoscopic navigation during free-breathing procedures, reducing workflow disruption and improving safety; demonstrates a practical fusion of volumetric rendering and patient-specific motion modeling applicable to other intraoperative imaging tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: static CT vs. dynamic CT-informed Gaussian splats with motion arrows showing airway deformation
Before/after registration heatmap or bar chart showing localization error (mm) with breath-hold vs. CT-informed dynamic rendering
Pipeline diagram: CT → Gaussian splats → respiratory motion field → dynamic render → video-to-CT registration
Clinical workflow illustration contrasting breath-hold protocol (disrupted workflow) vs. free-breathing dynamic navigation (streamlined)
paper_title: Stop Holding Your Breath: CT-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Bronchoscopy
paper_authors: Andrea Dunn Beltran, Daniel Rho, Aarav Mehta, Xinqi Xiong, Raúl San José Estépar
